evidence: One secret serves as both admin credential and webhook HMAC key. Unrelated.

panel.summary: Single secret reused as both the Yorkie admin API credential and the webhook HMAC key
panel.evidence: `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is sent verbatim as `authorization: API-Key <key>` to Yorkie's AdminService (yorkie-admin.service.ts:177) and is simultaneously the HMAC key for inbound webhook verification (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:30). This is Yorkie's own design (project SecretKey), so it is not introduced here, but it means one leaked value both authenticates the backend to Yorkie's admin API and lets an attacker forge `updatedAt` webhooks; rotation must be coordinated. Worth noting only — no separate secret is available upstream.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts::single secret reused as both the yorkie admin api credential and the webhook hmac key

coderabbit.detail: **Document the empty-PATCH exception.** This says every metadata update bumps `updatedAt`, but the implementation intentionally skips the bump for empty PATCH requests. Qualify this as “every non-empty metadata update” to keep the design contract accurate.
